title: runbook-diff-and-execution-simulator-integration
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Add runbook diff engine and safe execution simulator to incident-bot: enables preflight validation and deterministic rehearsal of on-call runbooks without contacting production systems.
description: Motivation: On-call runbooks change often and it's difficult to validate that a runbook will execute safely and produce the expected remediation steps before shipping. This PR introduces two tightly-coupled capabilities: (1) a runbook-diff engine that computes a semantic diff between two versions of a runbook (intent-aware, ignores formatting/noise, highlights changed steps that affect external calls), and (2) an execution-simulator that can rehearse runbooks against synthetic/recorded telemetry in a sandboxed environment to surface side-effects, missing guardrails, and timing regressions. Summary of changes: implements 'incident_bot.runbook.diff' with semantic AST-based diffing; adds 'incident_bot.simulator' with pluggable backends (replay, mocked-api, dry-run); wires new endpoints to the incident-bot CLI and web action menu; adds a rehearsal test harness and CI integration that runs simulation scenarios. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-13724) [x] unit tests for diff and simulator core [x] integration tests for CLI flow and web action [x] mocks for external services [x] documentation pages added in /docs/runbooks/simulation.md [x] rollout gating (feature-flagged) How it works: the diff engine tokenizes runbook steps into normalized operations (shell calls, API calls, wait/check steps) and builds a step graph; the semantic diff marks additions, deletions, and behavioral deltas (e.g., a shell->api change flagged as potentially higher risk). The simulator accepts a runbook and a scenario (telemetry snapshot or recorded trace) and executes each step against a sandbox adapter; adapters implement safe contracts: no network by default, optional recorded-replay mode for customer-provided traces, and a 'shadow' mode that forwards reads but blocks writes. Safety: all write operations are automatically stubbed unless the runbook opt-in header includes a signed test token; the simulator also enforces a max-step timeout and a resource-usage budget per rehearsal. Backwards compat: feature gated behind 'runbook_simulator' flag; no changes to existing runbook storage schemas. Commits: "feat(diff): add semantic runbook diff engine and graph normalizer"; "feat(sim): core execution-simulator with replay/mocked backends"; "feat(cli): add 'rehearse' and 'diff' subcommands to incident-bot CLI"; "test: add scenario fixtures and integration tests"; "docs: runbooks simulation guide and safety notes"; "chore: add CI job and gating for rehearsals" Changed files (high level): incident-bot/runbook/diff.py, incident-bot/simulator/core.py, incident-bot/simulator/adapters/replay_adapter.py, incident-bot/cli/rehearse.py, incident-bot/web/actions/runbook_rehearse_handler.py, tests/fixtures/telemetry/*, tests/integration/test_rehearse_flow.py, docs/runbooks/simulation.md, .github/workflows/rehearse.yml, packaging/feature_flags.yaml Testing & validation: added 24 unit tests (diff semantics, graph normalization), 6 integration scenarios that exercise typical production runbooks against recorded telemetry (auth-service outage, db failover, cache steward), and a synthetic noise scenario that verifies the diff engine ignores cosmetic changes. CI: initially flaked on a timing-dependent integration; added deterministic timers and retry logic; final CI run status: all checks passed (lint, unit, integration-rehearse, e2e-mock). Reviews & discussion: reviewers requested stricter sandboxing and clearer UX for unsafe steps; we added an explicit 'unsafe-steps' summary in the rehearsal output and an opt-in flow requiring a signed test token for any step that would perform writes. Rollout plan: merged behind feature flag; canary enabled for staging team; monitoring added to track rehearsal failures and simulator resource usage to prevent CI/infra impact. Migration notes: none required. Follow-ups: (a) add policy linter for runbook steps (ENG-13778) (b) expose rehearsal telemetry in Console as a per-run artifact (ENG-13790). Links: Linear ENG-13724 (design), SUP-2991 (support replication scenario), docs/runbooks/simulation.md.

review_comments: Ethan Brooks: Please enumerate what constitutes an 'unsafe' step in the README — reply: added 'unsafe-steps' section and examples.
Marta Ruiz: Sandbox adapters look good, but add time budget enforcement — reply: added per-step timeout and total budget enforcement with tests.
Jin Park: CI integration initially flaky due to non-deterministic timers — reply: switched to monotonic test timers and retries; re-ran CI.
Ops: request to surface rehearsal artifacts to S3 for retention — noted as follow-up (ENG-13790).
notes: Feature gated; to enable for a team add 'runbook_simulator: true' in packaging/feature_flags.yaml and restart the bot service.
Simulator resource usage is counted against 'rehearse_concurrency' in runtime config; default is 2 concurrent rehearsals per worker.
For customer replay scenarios we require a signed replay token to prevent accidental replaying of live PII-containing traces.
